questions.questionText: When was the African National Congress (ANC) founded?
questions.explanation: The ANC was founded on January 8, 1912, at a conference in Bloemfontein.

questions.questionText: What was the Defiance Campaign?
questions.explanation: The Defiance Campaign saw volunteers deliberately break unjust laws to challenge apartheid.

questions.questionText: Who was Nelson Mandela?

options.text: ANC leader who became first black President

questions.explanation: Mandela co-founded ANC Youth League, led armed resistance, was imprisoned for 27 years, became President in 1994.

questions.questionText: What was the Pan Africanist Congress (PAC)?

options.text: Split from ANC focusing on Africanist views

questions.explanation: PAC broke from ANC in 1959, rejecting non-racialism for African nationalism.

questions.questionText: What was the Rivonia Trial?

options.text: Trial where Mandela and others were sentenced to life imprisonment

questions.explanation: Rivonia Trial (1963-64) resulted in Mandela and other leaders receiving life sentences.

questions.questionText: When did Sharpeville massacre occur?
questions.explanation: Sharpeville massacre occurred when police opened fire on PAC anti-pass law protesters, killing 69.

questions.questionText: What was MK (Umkhonto we Sizwe)?

options.text: ANC's armed wing for sabotage operations

questions.explanation: MK (1961) conducted sabotage against government infrastructure to protest apartheid policies.

questions.questionText: How did the Freedom Charter (1955) reflect resistance goals?

options.text: Demanded democratic rights and equality for all South Africans

questions.explanation: The Freedom Charter declared South Africa belonged to all its people and demanded democratic rights.

questions.questionText: What role did women play in anti-apartheid resistance?

options.text: Led protests, supported networks, organized campaigns

questions.explanation: Women like Albertina Sisulu led mass women's mobilizations and supported underground networks.

questions.questionText: What was the role of the 1955 Congress of the People?

options.text: Adopted the Freedom Charter expressing people's demands

questions.explanation: The Congress brought together thousands to adopt the Freedom Charter, defining resistance goals.

questions.questionText: How did international pressure support resistance?

options.text: Sanctions isolated apartheid and boosted local resistance morale

questions.explanation: UN condemnation, cultural boycotts, and economic sanctions increased costs of apartheid and encouraged resistance.

questions.questionText: What was the significance of the Treason Trial (1956-1961)?

options.text: Tested whether Freedom Charter constituted treason

questions.explanation: Treason Trial's acquittal of all defendants demonstrated government's inability to criminalize resistance.

questions.questionText: What was the difference between ANC and PAC approaches?

options.text: PAC advocated African nationalism vs ANC's multi-racial approach

questions.explanation: PAC rejected ANC's non-racialism, arguing for African leadership without Indian and Coloured involvement.

questions.questionText: What was Operation Mayibuye?

options.text: Plan to rebuild non-racial South Africa

questions.explanation: Mayibuye was a vision for rebuilding South Africa through unity and reconstruction after apartheid.

questions.questionText: Analyze the evolution from non-violent to armed resistance.

options.text: Government repression led ANC to form MK after Sharpeville
Violence was always the primary strategy

questions.explanation: Banning of organizations, Sharpeville massacre, and state terror convinced ANC that violence was necessary.

questions.questionText: Evaluate the role of exiled activists in the struggle.

options.text: Maintained international awareness and coordinated external pressure

questions.explanation: Exiled leaders like Tambo built international support networks, diplomatic pressure, and external funding.

questions.questionText: To what extent did the Freedom Charter represent a unified vision?

options.text: Unified diverse groups but also contained tensions over class and race

questions.explanation: Freedom Charter united ANC, SACP, and Congress allies but later sparked PAC split over 'nationalist' interpretation.

questions.questionText: Analyze the relationship between religious institutions and resistance.

options.text: Some churches provided sanctuary while others justified apartheid

questions.explanation: While Dutch Reformed Church supported apartheid, black churches and theologians like Desmond Tutu opposed it.

questions.questionText: Evaluate the impact of resistance activities on the apartheid government.

options.text: Forced concessions, international isolation, and eventual negotiations
Had no impact on government policy

questions.explanation: Decades of resistance, combined with sanctions, made apartheid economically unsustainable and politically isolated.

questions.questionText: How did the Rivonia trial shape perceptions of the struggle?

options.text: Mandela's speech transformed him into global icon while exposing government oppression

questions.explanation: Mandela's speech from the dock, and his life imprisonment, made him a symbol of resistance worldwide.
